nodes.question: What percentage of temperate forests in South-Eastern Australia was affected by the fires in 2019/20?
nodes.answer: The fires affected 23% of temperate forests in South-Eastern Australia.
nodes.paragraph: In 2019/20, the hottest and driest years were recorded, and mega-fires burned uncontrolled for months. The fires affected 24 mil- lion hectares of forest (or 23% of temperate forests in South- Eastern Australia) (Abram et al. 2021 :1) and wreaked havoc on human and animal populations, with 33 people and over one billion animals killed. Climate change and climatic shocks such as drought, floods and fires have already had a direct impact on food production and with that, rural livelihoods. Australia S Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food modelling for the year 2021 showed a 23% reduction in farm prof - its due to changes in seasonal conditions (when compared to 1950 2000) with future climate change expected to see even tougher conditions (Hughes and Gooday 2021 ). nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is there a need to adopt better practices for managing vital resources in the Mediterranean?
nodes.answer: Better practices are needed to address the effects of climate change and the pressures on natural resources resulting from environmental challenges like droughts, wildfires, and flooding.
nodes.paragraph: Keywords Nature-based Solutions Bioeconomy WEFE nexus Multi-criteria Assessment Participatory Workshop et al. [full author details at the end of the article] 1 3 Circular Economy and SustainabilityIntroduction During the last decades, the Mediterranean basin has faced increased environmental chal - lenges related to climate change and increased urbanization [ 1]. Extensive droughts dur - ing summer have aggravated the desertification of the region [ 2] which, coupled with the subsequent wildfires and increased floodings, has put pressure on its natural resources. Cli - mate change effects ought to be addressed by adopting better practices for managing vital resources, such as water, energy, and food, as well as recognizing their interconnections. Based on the latter, in the last years, scientists, researchers, and policymakers have explored the Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystem nexus approach which emphasizes the interac - tions between those sectors and promotes integrated strategies [ 3, 4]. Strategies that deal with the effects of climate change while covering the WEFE nexus include the implemen - tation of Nature-based Solutions (NBS) [ 5, 6], and Bioeconomy Solutions (BES), which emphasize the importance of local natural resources and biowaste as part of the solution.

nodes.question: Why is Greece, particularly Attica, considered a climate change hotspot?
nodes.answer: Greece, particularly Attica, is considered a climate change hotspot because it is experiencing faster warming rates than the global average and has an increased occurrence of heat waves, prolonged droughts, and a heightened risk of forest fires.
nodes.paragraph: To meet these multifaceted goals, extensive and holistic mapping and assessment of all environmental pressures is needed, based on up-to-date and reliable information such as geospatial, remote sensing, in situ observational and numerical modelling data. Athens Metropolitan Area (AMA), which holds the 14th place in the European ranking for cities regarding population density (https:// ec. europa. eu/ euros tat/) in a country (Greece) where 80.36% (reference year 2022) of the population is liv - ing in urban areas ( https:// datab ank. world bank. org/) faces multiple pressures, among which urban climate variability, urban excess heat, air quality degradation, and lack of green spaces, prevail (Asprogerakas 2016).
